items.title: The Stock Market Is “Petrified of Oracle’s Balance Sheet” as Microsoft Walks Away
items.summary: Key TakeawaysMicrosoft is winding down a deal to rent AI computing power from Oracle, days after Oracle canceled an estimated $7 billion chip-leasing deal with Tencent. The Microsoft contract itself looks small, but losing it leaves Oracle’s backlog leaning even harder on OpenAI, which S&P says accounts for about half of it.

items.title: Credo Technology Group Holding (CRDO) Helped Set New AI Network Standards, Is The 44% Undervaluation Real?
items.summary: Credo Technology Group Holding (CRDO) has contributed to the delivery of two new Open Compute Project optical telemetry standards, created with Oracle and industry partners. These standards aim to support more reliable AI data center networks by enabling richer link monitoring. For investors watching Credo Technology Group Holding, the approval of these Open Compute Project standards lands after a sharp reset in sentiment. The share price has risen 7.3% over the last day but is still down...

items.title: ING Is Getting Cold Feet on the AI Boom
items.summary: ING is shopping $500 million in loans tied to US data center projects, including one connected to OpenAI-backed Stargate. The sale isn’t a distress signal, but it raises questions about who will finance AI’s increasingly expensive buildout.

items.title: Google Pushes New AI Chips. Why There Could Be an Opening.
items.summary: Alphabet’s Google is expanding its AI hardware lineup with systems designed for sensitive data and large workloads.

items.title: AMD Stock Could Jump 34%. No, It’s Got Nothing to Do With the Nvidia Turmoil.
items.summary: Oppenheimer analyst Rick Schafer expects AMD’s data-center sales to surge 135% next year thanks to robust AI spending.

items.title: Cloudflare Jumps 11%, Nebius Surges 9% as AI Cloud Stocks Defy NVIDIA’s Slide; CoreWeave Rallies 6% on Wayve Deal
items.summary: While NVIDIA slides on a startling report about its CEO, the cloud companies that buy its chips are drawing buyers back. One of them just posted what its CEO calls a best-ever quarter, but a few numbers underneath complicate the celebration.

items.title: Nvidia Isn’t Staying in The $180s for Long
items.summary: A political earthquake in Washington and a boardroom investigation into its CEO have rattled Nvidia shares, yet analysts keep raising their numbers. Two upcoming answers could decide which side of this standoff turns out to be right.
